author: sonnet
label: seeded-06-01
changes: Rewrote the plan as a short paragraph, terms, 7 steps, a failure table and open questions, so the file alone answers all eight questions.
Defined the 10,000-row threshold as a comparison with unfiltered reports.row_count (Q1).
Stated small exports read the replica and create no record (Q2).
Large POST returns 202 with export_id; added a GET latest endpoint and 5-second polling so the page learns the id (Q3).
Listed report_exports columns and who changes each status (Q4).
Defined duplicate as same user and report, enforced by a unique partial index, returning the existing export with 200 (Q5).
Spelled out retry behaviour: restart from row one, same record and key, status stays running, abort own upload (Q6).
Failure email and failed status both come from on_final_failure after the last attempt (Q7).
Explained signed link: 24 h bearer link made at email time, file kept 7 days by the lifecycle rule (Q8).
Added memory approach (8 MB buffer, one batch), idempotent stop when already done, enqueue-failure handling.
Added open questions on the 30-minute timeout, bearer link security and no fresh link after the email.
Added a short account of how the current page works (replica only, permission check, 500-row keyset paging) and the 900 MB / 2M row size to the opening paragraph.

Expanded Terms: added view state (why the click must send filters), send_email, and multipart upload as its own term; added queue details (512 MB workers, 64 KB payload, on_final_failure once); noted reports.row_count is the only stored size.

Added rules the earlier version lacked as rules: one active export per user/report, job never holds a whole report in memory and must finish within the timeout, half-written file never downloadable, no cleanup job.
Renamed Steps to How it runs; reordered step 6 so the reason for the latest endpoint (learning export_id after reload) comes before polling.
Added an explicit enqueue-fails row to the failure table; merged repeated wording in the failure rows.
Cut the repeated statement of the 7-day vs 24-hour link relationship to one line in step 5, and the repeated 'expires first' reasoning.
Kept all original facts: threshold 10,000, 202/200/500 responses, 8 MB buffer, ~110 parts, 5 s polling, key format, template name, rollout order, out-of-scope list, and the three open questions.
